verdicts.detail: The 20% deductions are right (pp.41, 57). But 'security forfeited without a SLLIA' overstates the rule and has no cite. §25.194(d)(3)(E) forfeits the intermediate-agreement security only when the customer neither withdraws before the SLLIA deadline nor executes a SLLIA. A customer that withdraws before the study begins, or that is allocated zero MW and withdraws before the deadline, gets the full balance back less amounts owed ((d)(3)(B), p.40). One allocated part of its demand that withdraws before the deadline loses 20% ((d)(3)(C)).
verdicts.corrected_value: 16 TAC §25.194: full return (less amounts owed) on withdrawal before ERCOT begins the study, or when allocated zero MW and withdrawing before the SLLIA deadline; 20% of the security for allocated capacity kept on withdrawal before the SLLIA deadline; intermediate-agreement security forfeited if the customer neither withdraws before the SLLIA deadline nor executes a SLLIA; 20% of the security for withdrawn contracted demand kept after a SLLIA; CIAC not refundable
verdicts.words: (E) Forfeiture. A large load customer that does not withdraw its interconnection request before the deadline to execute a SLLIA and does not execute a SLLIA before the deadline set forth in subsection (f) of this section is deemed to have forfeited any financial security that the large load customer posted under an intermediate agreement.
